The Fifth Derivative of the Expected Information

Source: R/d5expected_hessian.R
distrib_d5expected_hessian.Rd

Returns \(\partial^5\,\mathbb{E}[\ell_{ab}]/\partial\theta_c\, \partial\theta_d\,\partial\theta_e\,\partial\theta_f\,\partial\theta_g\), with one component per pair \((a,b)\) and per unordered quintuple \((c,d,e,f,g)\).

Usage

distrib_d5expected_hessian(
  distrib,
  y,
  theta,
  scale = c("parameter", "link"),
  method = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

distrib

A distribution object inheriting from distrib.

y

A numeric vector of observations.

theta

A named list of parameters; each has length 1 or length(y).

scale

"parameter" or "link".

method

NULL (the default) or an object inheriting from ExpectMethod, as for distrib_d4expected_hessian(). See expected_derivative_methods.

...

Passed to methods; the default method accepts accuracy, the order of accuracy of the stencil passed to numericals7::fd_tensor() (4 by default).

Value

A named list of numeric vectors, keyed as d5expected_names(distrib@params).

Details

The components are symmetric in \((a,b)\) and in \((c,d,e,f,g)\) separately, and are keyed by d5expected_names().

No family computes this order in closed form. The default method applies one tensor-product central stencil of numericals7::fd_tensor() to the highest derivative of the expected information that the family computes itself: a first difference of distrib_d4expected_hessian() for the univariate families shipped with the package, which compute the fourth order in closed form, and for a wrapper of such a family; a stencil of order two on distrib_d3expected_hessian() or of order three on distrib_d2expected_hessian() for a family that registers only those. A wrapper never differences from an order above the one of the family that it wraps, since its own orders are built from the parent's. A family without an analytic second derivative of its expected information signals an error, as it does for the third and fourth orders. The step of a stencil of order \(r\) is \(\varepsilon^{1/(r+4)}\max(1, |x|)\) in the coordinate \(x\), reduced so that every node stays inside the domain.

On scale = "link" the stencil is taken in the linear predictors, on the link-scale fourth derivative, which distrib_d4expected_hessian() computes exactly from the analytic orders and the derivatives of the inverse links. A stencil on the parameter scale composed with the lower orders by Leibniz's rule and the Faa di Bruno formula would need the sixth derivative of the inverse links, and was measured against 50-digit references and rejected: where a parameter is small the terms of the composition cancel, and the stencil's error is amplified up to a relative error of 6e-3, against 2e-9 or better for the stencil in \(\eta\). The method reads scale and returns the scale that it is given.

With an object as method, the result is the derivative of the matrix that the method defines, computed as for the lower orders by Leibniz's formula for expect_opg() and with the moved density for expect_integrate() and expect_mc(). It reads observed derivatives up to the sixth (distrib_deriv6()), so only identity = "score" is available; the Hessian identity would need the seventh order and signals an error. On the link scale the polynomial is evaluated with the observed derivatives on the link scale, for the same reason: the identities and the moved density hold in any coordinates.

See also

distrib_d4expected_hessian() for the order below, d5expected_names(), distrib_deriv6()

Examples

d <- poisson_distrib()
str(distrib_d5expected_hessian(d, 2, list(mu = 3), scale = "link"))
#> List of 1
#>  $ mu_mu_mu_mu_mu_mu_mu: num -3

g <- gaussian1_distrib()
r <- distrib_d5expected_hessian(g, 0, list(mu = 0, sigma = 2))
r[["sigma_sigma_sigma_sigma_sigma_sigma_sigma"]]
#> [1] 11.25
